states.content: For the TEE-guided cardioversion, pre-procedure prep is nothing by mouth after midnight except small sips of water with approved morning medications. Approved morning medications: take apixaban 5 mg in the morning with a sip of water, take metoprolol tartrate 37.5 mg, and hold lisinopril until after the procedure; magnesium can be taken tonight, not tomorrow morning. Marcus Reed should avoid NSAIDs and may use acetaminophen if he needs something for pain. Pharmacist Klein's reconciliation confirms lisinopril 10 mg daily is held tomorrow morning and magnesium oxide 400 mg is taken nightly for the five-night course. Pre-procedure checklist for Marcus Reed: last apixaban dose this morning, metoprolol taken, lisinopril held, no food since midnight, no new bleeding symptoms, and no NSAIDs. Marcus Reed confirmed to nurse Jamison that all checklist details are correct.

states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. Because the timing of his Monday-night apixaban dose is uncertain, Dr. Patel is changing the approach from direct cardioversion to TEE-guided cardioversion so a clot can be checked for first while still avoiding an unnecessary delay. The Wednesday, March 11 slot was released, and the Thursday, March 12 slot was taken by an add-on case; the TEE-guided cardioversion is now scheduled for Friday, March 13 at 12:30 PM with 11:00 AM arrival at the cardiac procedures unit on the third floor. Reception Ana has reconfirmed the Friday arrival: March 13, 11:00 AM, cardiac procedures unit, third floor. Scheduler Terry has updated the arrival letter in the portal, and Marcus's own portal copy prep line now says TEE-guided cardioversion. Marcus requests that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion, and to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed without missing any further doses. Pharmacist Klein confirms apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit. Post-procedure follow-up note entered: Monday, March 16 nurse callback at 8:40 AM; Tuesday, March 17 ECG at 11:00 AM followed by a Dr. Patel visit at 11:30 AM in Suite 4C. Marcus has said these follow-up times work for him right now and asked that they be kept in the portal.

states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list. Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Dr. Patel has now instructed Marcus to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and to use acetaminophen instead if needed, because NSAIDs raise bleeding risk with apixaban. Pharmacist Klein reinforced this: no ibuprofen or naproxen while Marcus is on apixaban. Dr. Patel instructs Marcus to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed and not miss any further doses. Marcus reported he has not missed any morning apixaban doses and no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers; he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations but still took that pill before bed. Marcus is pretty sure he took his Monday-night apixaban dose, but it was late and he cannot prove the time. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Marcus does not drink energy drinks.

His presentation is characterized as symptomatic atrial fibrillation/flutter with exertional dyspnea and lightheadedness, and no active bleeding.
